title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah pays tributes to Sree Narayana Guru Ji on his Jayanti
subtitle:
Shri Amit Shah also pays tributes to Mahatma Ayyankali Ji on his jayanti
Sree Narayana Guru Ji showed the path to build a more harmonious, just and benevolent society through spirituality
His principles of knowledge, compassion, equality and spiritual freedom continue to inspire us on our path to India's greatness
Ayyankali Ji was a pioneering social reformer who paved the way for social transformation through education in Keralam
body_text:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah pays tributes to Sree Narayana Guru Ji on his Jayanti. Shri Amit Shah also pays tributes to Mahatma Ayyankali Ji on his Jayanti.
In his post on X platform, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said “Sree Narayana Guru Ji showed the path to build a more harmonious, just and benevolent society through spirituality. His principles of knowledge, compassion, equality and spiritual freedom continue to inspire us on our path to India's greatness. My solemn tributes to the great seer on his jayanti.”
In another post, Shri Amit Shah said “I bow to the great sage Mahatma Ayyankali Ji on his Jayanti. Ayyankali Ji was a pioneering social reformer who paved the way for social transformation through education in Keralam. He also laid the foundation of a united and robust society upholding the values of social justice and equity. His values continue to guide our path to the pinnacle of progress.”

enrichment.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah paid tribute on social media to Sree Narayana Guru Ji and Mahatma Ayyankali Ji on their respective Jayantis. He praised Sree Narayana Guru for promoting spirituality, knowledge, compassion and equality, and lauded Ayyankali Ji as a pioneering social reformer who advanced education and social justice in Kerala.
enrichment.context: Sree Narayana Guru (1856-1928) and Ayyankali (1863-1941) were prominent social reformers from Kerala who worked to dismantle caste-based discrimination and untouchability in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Sree Narayana Guru founded the SNDP Yogam and promoted the ideal 'One Caste, One Religion, One God for Mankind', while Ayyankali led movements for the rights of Dalits, including access to education and public roads, and later served in the Sree Mulam Popular Assembly. Such tribute messages from political leaders on the birth anniversaries of historical social reformers are routine occurrences in India's public discourse and do not reflect any new policy announcement.
